subject: Post-call: Paywise — access model & retention clarifications
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@paywise.com>, Tom Saunders <tom.saunders@paywise.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Paywise — access model & retention clarifications

Thanks for the call earlier today — quick recap and the open items we promised to follow up on. Great discussion; primary objectives for Paywise were: minimize access footprint for support, meet EU data residency for sensitive PII flows, and retain audit logs for 12 months.

High-level recap (TL;DR):
- Support access: Redwood provides RBAC roles + temporary JIT elevation via break-glass flow.
- Data residency: Hosted regions can be pinned to eu-west-1 for EU-sensitive data; tokens & logs can be routed accordingly.
- Retention & logging: Full per-request audit trail available (request metadata + token counts). We can configure 12 months retention for logs; standard retention is 90 days.

Open items / asklist (we'll own the first two items):
1) Customer asks around PII classification — can you share the list of fields you consider sensitive? (Paywise)
2) Confirm whether support engineers should have read-only access to archived payloads or only metadata (Paywise) — we can model both.
3) Security team wants a written outline of the break-glass procedure and controls (Redwood to provide).
4) Requested example audit log entries and retention SLA (Redwood to provide).

Attachments I’m including: support-access-overview.pdf (high-level RBAC + break-glass flow). Also linking the RBAC roles CSV and the break-glass playbook in the follow-up.

Next steps:
- Paywise: share sensitive-field list and confirm intended residency for tokens & logs.
- Redwood: circulate break-glass playbook, RBAC roles CSV, and sample audit log lines by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks — happy to hop on another 30m if you'd like a walkthrough of the playbook.

—
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@paywise.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Saunders <tom.saunders@paywise.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Paywise — access model & retention clarifications

Thanks Karthik — helpful summary. A few clarifying Qs before we hand anything to our security folks: 

1) Sensitive fields: we classify account_number, ssn_partial, full_name, and transaction_details as sensitive. We'll attach a CSV of fields in a follow-up.

2) Support access: Our operating model prefers metadata-only for tier-1 support (session ids, error traces, request timestamps). Tier-2 (engineering) may need ephemeral read access for payloads, but only after explicit approval and only for the timeframe required to triage. How does Redwood's JIT elevation capture approvals and scope the session?

3) Break-glass audit: our auditors want proof that break-glass events require a second approver and generate immutable evidence (who approved, justification, timestamp). Does Redwood store the approval artifact in the audit trail?

Also — can you confirm whether logs with PII can be redacted at ingestion and still satisfy our debug needs?

—
Lina Gomez
Head of Product Security | Paywise
Lina.Gomez@paywise.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@paywise.com>, Tom Saunders <tom.saunders@paywise.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Paywise — access model & retention clarifications

Hi Lina — great questions, answers inline below. Summarizing for your auditors as well.

1) Sensitive fields — noted. Please attach the CSV when convenient and we’ll map field-level redaction and tokenization options. We support both deterministic tokenization and one-way hashing depending on your desire to preserve searchability.

2) JIT elevation / approvals — Redwood’s break-glass flow works like this:
- Requestor (engineer) opens elevation request via Console or API.
- Request includes justification + target session id(s) and TTL.
- Required approver(s): configurable per-customer; defaults to two approvers for customers who enable "strict approval".
- Approval artifacts: approvals are recorded as signed events (audit entry includes approver id, timestamp, and justification). We store the approval artifact as part of the immutable audit stream.

3) Break-glass evidence — yes, each event yields an immutable audit record. We can also attach the approving approver's SSO assertion ID if you want stronger binding to your identity provider.

4) Redaction at ingestion — supported. Tradeoffs: full redaction removes payloads from logs which reduces root-cause signal. Pattern we recommend: ingest redacted payloads by default, enable temporary unredaction tokens for Tier-2 investigations tied to JIT approval, and persist the unredacted copy only to an isolated forensic store with separate retention (can be shorter than 12 months).

Attachments referenced below: breakglass-playbook.md (attached) and rbac-roles-csv.csv (link to Drive). Also included a sample audit log line in the body.

Sample audit entry (single line JSON):
{"timestamp":"2027-06-23T16:12:03Z","actor":"svc-support-joe@redwood.ai","action":"elevation.request","target":"session-0a1b2c","approved_by":["id:marissa.cole@redwood.ai","id:security-admin@paywise.com"],"ttl_seconds":3600,"justification":"Investigating failure on payment-retry"}

If that aligns, Marissa / Monica — can you share the RBAC CSV and the playbook artifacts I promised? We'll also produce a short redaction-vs-debugging appendix to send to Paywise security.

Happy to set a 30m follow-up with your security team this week.

—
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Post-call: Paywise — access model & retention clarifications

Quick follow-up with the artifacts attached and a short checklist for your security reviewers. Attachments: support-access-overview.pdf, breakglass-playbook.md, rbac-roles-csv.csv

Paywise security checklist (summary):
- Confirm residency scope: set logs & token storage to EU region (eu-west-1).
- RBAC model: see roles CSV. We recommend Tier-1 (support_readonly), Tier-2 (support_investigate), Tier-3 (engineering_admin).
- JIT policy: require two approvers for Tier-2 unredaction; approvals recorded in immutable audit stream.
- Retention: primary audit logs — 12 months (per request); forensic unredacted store — 90 days by default unless you specify otherwise.
- Evidence for auditors: we can produce a bundle (signed audit entries + SSO assertion hashes + playbook) on request; propose a 2-week lead time for the bundle.

Next steps for closure:
1) Lina/Tom: confirm EU residency and attach the sensitive-fields CSV.
2) Paywise security: confirm approval policy (single vs two approvers).
3) Redwood: we'll prepare the redaction appendix and provide HubSpot link to the deal checklist.

Links: RBAC roles (Drive): https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c-paywise-rbac
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/67890
